s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent urinary retention and sepsis with diffuse bladder wall thickening
salient_findings: Diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall
Diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation with comma-shaped nuclei
Dense, perivascular spindle cell proliferation with prominent cytological atypia
key_facts: 50-year-old man with known neurofibromatosis type 1
Multiple cutaneous neurofibromas
No history of smoking
Admitted for recurrent urinary retention and sepsis
Transurethral resection of the prostate revealed fibroleiomyomatous hyperplasia
Urinary function did not improve after transurethral resection
CT scan showed diffuse irregular polypoid thickening of the entire bladder wall
Cystoprostatectomy was performed due to compromised bladder function
Bladder wall was diffusely thickened, firm, and gray–white on gross examination
Near–complete loss of the detrusor muscle
Tumor cells were positive for S100, p16, neurofilaments, and CD56
Tumor cells were negative for pan-cytokeratin, EMA, MDM2, p63, ALK, CD117, DOG1, myogenin, desmin, and smooth muscle actin

shortlist.label: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neurofibromatosis type 1 and tumor cells are positive for S100 and neurofilaments

shortlist.label: Neurofibrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neurofibromatosis type 1 and histologic evaluation revealed a diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation

shortlist.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neurofibromatosis type 1 and multiple cutaneous neurofibromas, but this option is less likely given the malignant features

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Tumor cells are positive for S100, but this option is less likely given the malignant features and infiltrative growth pattern

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic evaluation revealed a diffuse bland spindle cell proliferation, but this option is less likely given the patient's history and tumor location

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of neurofibromatosis type 1 and the tumor cells are positive for S100 and neurofilaments, which are characteristic of nerve sheath tumors. The presence of cytological atypia, frequent mitoses, and an infiltrative growth pattern also supports a malignant diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neurofibrosarcoma
rejected.why: This term is sometimes used interchangeably with malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor, but it is not a preferred term in this context.

rejected.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
rejected.why: This is a type of benign neurofibroma that can occur in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1, but it does not typically exhibit the cytological atypia and infiltrative growth pattern seen in this case.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: This is a type of benign nerve sheath tumor that can occur in patients with neurofibromatosis type 2, but it is not typically malignant and does not exhibit the same level of cytological atypia and infiltrative growth as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: This is a type of tumor that can occur in the bladder, but it does not typically exhibit the same immunohistochemical profile as seen in this case, and it is not typically associated with neurofibromatosis type 1.
